lang.label: Language
nav.label: Sections
signin.title: Sign in
signin.text: Sign in with your web login name and password. No password yet, or forgot it? Send /web to Argus on another channel (Telegram): it answers with a link that signs you in once, within ten minutes, and lets you set one.
signin.limited: Too many failed attempts. Wait a quarter of an hour, or use a /web link.
approvals.approveAll: All of this kind, this run
approvals.gone: That question was answered or expired already.
checkpoint.title: possible loop
checkpoint.text: After {steps} steps, the loop checker says: {reason} Go on?
schedule.none: Nothing scheduled. /cron in the chat adds a schedule.
chat.title: Chat
chat.hint: The same as the Telegram chat: plain text goes to the active project or the front desk, /commands run.
settings.keysHint: A key is checked with the provider before it is saved, and used from the next request.
settings.toolsHint: off: not offered to the agent · deny · ask: you are asked · allow: runs unasked
settings.instructionsHint: What each project is told to do, in its system prompt on every request. Saving applies from its next request; an empty text removes them.
password.title: Web password
password.none: You have no web password yet. Choose a login name and a password of at least 10 characters to sign in without a /web link.
password.has: Your login name is {login}. Changing the password signs out your other sessions.
password.reset: You signed in with a /web link: for ten minutes you can set a new password without the current one.
password.saved: Saved. Your other sessions are signed out.
password.short: The password needs at least 10 characters.
password.badLogin: A login name is 2 to 64 letters, digits or . _ @ -
users.title: Users
users.inviteHint: Creates an operator and gives a sign-in link valid 24 hours, to send them. With it they set a web password; from the web they can connect Telegram.
users.name: Name
channels.title: Your channels
channels.hint: To use Argus from Telegram too, ask for a code and send it to the bot as /link <code> within 10 minutes.
projects.missing: There is no project {id} (or it is archived).
system.title: System
system.panicHint: Panic stops every run, rejects what is queued and refuses new work until you resume.
system.panicked: Everything is stopped (panic). Resume to accept work again.
setup.adminText: There is no admin yet. Create the admin's account: the login name and password you will sign in with. The link works once.
setup.invalid: This setup link is no longer valid. Run argus setup-link on the server for a new one.
setup.title: Set up Argus
setup.intro: What a new install needs, step by step. Every step runs a chat command, and each can be changed later in Settings.
setup.adminDone: You are the admin, signing in as {login}.
setup.keyHint: No agent can run without one. The key is checked with the provider before it is saved.
setup.modelsHint: The model a task runs on, and the front desk's. The defaults are fine to start with.
setup.telegramHint: To use Argus from Telegram as well: save the bot token from @BotFather (the bot starts at once), then connect your Telegram account with a code.
setup.projectHint: A project is an agent with its own folder, memory, model and budget. A template gives it instructions to start from; edit them on the project's page.
setup.systemText: Timezone {timezone}; every project may spend ${day} a day and ${month} a month unless set otherwise. These are in ops.yaml (timezone, budgets) and apply after a restart; /budget changes one budget at once.
setup.banner: Argus is not fully set up yet: it needs a provider key and a first project.
signin.codeText: Enter the 6-digit code from your authenticator app, or one of your recovery codes.
signin.badCode: That code is not right, or it was used already. After five wrong codes, start again.
totp.title: Authenticator code
totp.off: Off. With it on, every sign-in also asks for a 6-digit code from an authenticator app (Aegis, Google Authenticator, 1Password…). It is required when the web is public.
totp.required: This web interface is public: set up an authenticator code before anything else.
totp.scan: Add this key to your authenticator app (on a phone, the link opens it), then enter the code it shows.
totp.badCode: That code is not right. Check the phone’s clock, and try the next code.
totp.recovery: On. Keep these recovery codes somewhere safe: each one signs you in once without the phone. They are not shown again.
totp.on: On: every sign-in asks for a code. To turn it off, enter a code.
totp.onPublic: On. It is required while the web is public.
projects.mailHint: Argus sends the project's mail with an account only the admin sets; the agent never sees it. A mail goes unasked only to a trusted address within its counts; every other mail waits in the outbox for a person.
projects.gitHint: Argus clones, pulls and pushes for the project; its token never reaches the agent. Each remote has its own token.
projects.uploaded: Saved as {path}. Tell the project where it is.
palette.title: Search
palette.button: Search a project, a page or an action
palette.placeholder: Go to a project, a page, an action…
palette.keys: ↑ ↓ to move · Enter to open · Esc to close
approvals.denied: Denied. The agent is told no.
approvals.alwaysDone: Approved, and “{rule}” is allowed in {project} from now on.
ask.title: Ask Argus
ask.noProjectHint: The default model, for one job.
ask.placeholderTask: E.g.: Compare three hosting providers and make me a table.
ask.placeholderProject: E.g.: Put the holiday hours on the site.
attention.title: Waiting for you
attention.pausedText: Today: {spent}. It resumes tomorrow, or when you raise the budget.
home.never: Nothing yet: send it a first message
home.invalid: Not running: its settings do not validate
home.newHint: From a template: a site, research, documents
home.emptyText: A project is an agent with its own folder, memory, model and budget. Start one.
inbox.sub: Everything waiting for a decision, from every project, oldest first.
inbox.emptyText: The projects work on their own. You are told here and on Telegram.
newProject.idHint: Lower-case letters, digits and dashes. It is also the folder's name.
newProject.descriptionPlaceholder: E.g.: Runs the online shop and answers orders
newProject.blank: The defaults; you choose the rest
newProject.created: {id} is ready. Send it a first message.
cron.whatPlaceholder: E.g.: Send me yesterday's traffic report
cron.custom: A cron line of your own
cron.afterSave: Its next runs show after saving.
cron.none: No schedule yet: add one on the right.
cron.say.monthly: On day {date} of each month at {time}
trig.fromHint: Exact addresses or @domain, separated by commas.
trig.subject: Subject contains (optional)
trig.help: Checked in code, without the model: a run starts only for a new matching mail, and the agent reads it with mail_read. Mail already in the mailbox does not count. At most {perHour} runs an hour.
trig.whatPlaceholder: E.g.: Process the order in mail {{mail.id}} and draft the reply.
trig.status: Checked {check} · last match {match} · {runs}/{perHour} runs this hour
files.dropHint: They land in inbox/ · up to 2 GB
files.more: More files than shown: download the folder as a zip.
files.pick: Pick a file on the left to see it here.
sessions.sub: Conversations with no project, on the default model. Each remembers only while it is open, and closes a day after its last message, with its folder.
sessions.emptyText: Ask for something that belongs to no project. It runs in a folder of its own, and you can go on with it for a day.
sessions.first: Write what you need. Follow-ups go to the same conversation.
sessions.placeholder: Write a message… (Enter sends, Shift+Enter a new line)
space.label: The project's space
space.empty: Nothing yet. Tell {id} what to do: it works in its own folder and remembers between conversations.
space.placeholder: Write to {id}… (Enter sends, Shift+Enter a new line, files can be dropped here)
thread.label: The conversation
thread.uploaded: {path} uploaded; it is named in your message.
ps.descriptionHelp: One sentence. Shown on its card, and it tells the agent what the project is.
ps.modelHelp: The model it works with. The price is per million tokens, in and out.
ps.addProvider: Add a provider or a model…
ps.fallback: Model for when the budget runs low
ps.fallbackHelp: Used past the soft limit when its action is to switch to a cheaper model.
ps.progressHelp: A line in the conversation at each important step while it works.
ps.template: It follows the {template} template: what it does not set itself comes from there.
ps.toolsHelp: What it may do on its own, and what it asks you first. Off: it does not have the tool at all.
ps.toolHelp.read: Open and search the files in its folder.
ps.toolHelp.write: Create and change files in its folder.
ps.toolHelp.shell: Commands in a terminal, in the sandbox: builds, tests, scripts.
ps.toolHelp.web: Search the web and read public pages.
ps.toolHelp.agents: Start helper agents for parts of a task.
ps.toolHelp.git: Commit, push and pull to the remotes set below.
ps.toolHelp.mail: Only to the allowed addresses, and never without asking.
ps.toolHelp.mail_read: Its mailbox, when it has one: list, read, save attachments, mark as read. Never deletes or moves.
ps.toolHelp.other: Tools of extensions and MCP servers that have no rule of their own.
ps.widen.any: From now on it does this without asking you.
ps.widen.shell: From now on it runs any command in its sandbox without asking you.
ps.widen.web: From now on it reads any public site without asking you.
ps.widen.git: From now on it pushes without asking you.
ps.widen.mail_read: From now on it reads its mailbox without asking you.
ps.widen.write: From now on it changes its files without asking you.
ps.autoAllowHelp: Even when running commands asks: an exact command, or one that starts with it.
ps.webHostsHelp: Empty: any public site. Private addresses are always refused.
ps.approvalTimeoutHelp: Unanswered by then, it counts as a no.
ps.extensionsHelp: Programs installed once on the server; each project turns them on.
ps.extensionNetwork: Reaches the network, through the egress proxy.
ps.mcpHelp: Outside services whose tools the agent uses.
ps.resetHomeHelp: Its logins and caches go; it starts clean.
ps.oauthHelp: After adding it, Connect opens the provider's sign-in. Google and Slack need a client of yours, under Settings.
ps.localHelp: It runs confined: it reads the system and the project's folder, and keeps its files in a folder of its own.
ps.serverAdded: {name} is added. It is used from the next message.
ps.tokenHelp: Saved for this project and this remote only; the agent never sees it.
ps.mailboxNone: None: the project cannot read mail. An imaps:// account, or the default.
ps.readFoldersHelp: Only these folders of the mailbox; INBOX by default.
ps.mailNone: None: nothing can be sent until one is set.
ps.recipientsHelp: Exact addresses, or @domain for anyone there. Empty: nobody.
ps.trustedHelp: Exact addresses, each with how many mails a day it may get without a person being asked. Anyone else is asked about first.
ps.mailLimitsHelp: Recipients, not mails, over the last 24 hours. Used: {total} in all, {unattended} unasked.
ps.unaskedOn: On: trusted addresses get mail within their counts.
ps.paused: Paused: every mail is asked about (or refused) until resumed.
ps.pausedAuto: Paused by itself after 3 failed mails in a row: every mail is asked about until resumed.
ps.outboxHelp: Mails that waited for a person, newest first.
ps.outboxWaiting: A waiting mail is answered in the inbox, or where it was asked.
ps.outboxEmpty: Empty: no mail has waited for a person.
ps.budgetHelp: What it may spend, and when a run stops.
ps.softPctHelp: Past it, what is chosen below happens.
ps.maxStepsHelp: A run that reaches it stops.
ps.delegateHelp: Limits for an agent an extension runs for this project (Claude Code). The project's agent cannot raise them.
ps.delegateModelHelp: Sonnet fits most code work and spends a subscription slowest; Opus for the hardest tasks. Another model id: Advanced.
ps.memoryHelp: What it remembers between conversations, and the points its files can go back to.
ps.userProfileHelp: How you like to work, across projects.
ps.undoHelp: The folder as it was before each run.
ps.resetHelp: It forgets the conversation; its memory, files and schedules stay.
ps.archiveHelp: It stops; its files stay and it can come back.
ps.advancedHelp: Every key of the project's file, with its default. A key marked as the project's own no longer follows its template.
ps.saved: Saved. {id} uses it from its next message.
sys.sub: Everything that is Argus's rather than one project's. Nothing to write in a file.
sys.resetHelp: Remove it from ops.yaml: the default applies again.
sys.restartNeeded: Some changes apply after a restart
sys.restartByHand: Restart Argus by hand: it runs without Docker or systemd.
sys.accessHelp: Where this page opens from. Any install starts private; you can change it whenever you want.
sys.modeHelp.private: Only on the server: you reach it through an SSH tunnel or a VPN.
sys.modeHelp.tailscale: From your phone and laptop, over HTTPS, with no port open and no password.
sys.modeHelp.public: On a domain of yours, from anywhere. The authenticator code is required.
sys.privateHow: On your computer, open a tunnel, then http://127.0.0.1:3091:
sys.publicWarnTitle: Anyone on the internet sees the sign-in page.
sys.publicWarn: Whoever gets in controls the agents, the keys and the budget. Public mode requires the authenticator code, ends idle sessions, and needs HTTPS in front (Caddy, in the compose overlay).
sys.publicGuide: How to set it up safely
sys.idleMinutes: Minutes idle before signing out (public mode)
sys.modelsHelp: The providers with a key or none needed, and their models. A model needs a price: from the catalogs, or one you give.
sys.noProviders: No provider can run a model yet: add one.
sys.defaultsHelp: For sessions and tasks, and for the loop checker. They apply at once.
sys.catalogHelp: Its models and prices come from the catalog, refreshed daily. The key is checked with the provider before it is saved.
sys.providerAdded: {name} is added. It applies after a restart.
sys.priceHelp: USD per million tokens. Leave empty when a public list has its price.
sys.modelAdded: {name} is added. It applies after a restart.
sys.secretsHelp: Every secret something needs, in one place. Saved encrypted, never shown again: replace or remove it.
sys.valueHelp: It is saved encrypted and never shown again.
sys.signInHelp: This opens the provider's sign-in, in the browser where you are signed in to Argus.
sys.secretNameHelp: Capital letters, digits and _. Settings name it as ${NAME}. Names starting with ARGUS_ are reserved.
sys.searchHelp: Who answers the agents' searches. Each search is charged to the project that searched.
sys.searchHelp.deepseek: the default, through the DeepSeek key
sys.searchKeyMissing: Missing: search does not work without it.
sys.searchKeySet: Saved. Replacing it checks it with one search.
sys.extensionsHelp: Programs installed once on the server; each project turns them on in its settings.
sys.otherRepoHelp: A git repository with an extension.yaml: https://…#folder@ref. Before installing, you are shown what it asks for.
sys.ext.office: Word, Excel and PowerPoint: create, read, edit; screenshots and PDF.
sys.ext.browser: A headless Chromium: dynamic pages, forms, screenshots. The public internet only.
sys.ext.pdf: Merge, split, extract text and images.
sys.ext.media: Audio and video with ffmpeg; downloads with yt-dlp.
sys.templatesHelp: A new project's starting settings. A change reaches the projects that follow it, except where a project set the value itself.
sys.reach: A change reaches {projects}, in what they do not set themselves.
sys.templateInstructions: What a new project starts with; projects that exist keep theirs.
sys.budgetsHelp: What every project together may spend, and a new project's budget.
sys.telegramHelp: The bot's token is under Keys and secrets.
sys.languageHelp: Each user picks the interface's language at the top; it is kept for them. What Argus writes itself (command answers, Telegram) stays in English for now.
sys.addPackHelp: A JSON file with the English texts translated; a text it lacks shows in English.
sys.codeFirst: Write the language's code first (de, pt-BR).
sys.advancedHelp: Every key of {file}, with its default. data_dir, config_dir and dsh_home are changed by hand, with Argus stopped.
sys.findKey: Find a key: web, limits, scheduler…
sys.usersHelp: The admin changes the settings; an operator works in the projects. Linking a Tailscale login lets a person in from their own devices with no password.
sys.tailscaleLoginHelp: As Tailscale shows it: you@github, you@example.com. Empty removes it.
sys.ts1: On the server, put Argus on your tailnet
sys.ts1Help: It installs Tailscale (asking first), signs the server in to your account, and publishes Argus with HTTPS. It prints the address.
sys.ts2: Set the public address below to that address
sys.ts2Help: Then open it from a phone or laptop signed in to the same Tailscale account.
sys.ts3: Turn on sign-in with Tailscale, and link each person's login
sys.ts3Help: Linked people come in with no password; nobody else does.
sys.sessionsHelp: Every browser signed in as you. End the ones you do not know, then change your password.
glob.schedulesSub: Every schedule, from every project. A new one is made in its project's space.
glob.costsSub: Every request to a model, charged to the project that made it.
costs.notionalHelp: What agents on a subscription (Claude Code) would have cost at the API's list prices. Not charged, not counted against the budget.
